art-residencies.headline: America's Future Fall 2026 Virtual Writing Fellowship
art-residencies.summary: America's Future is accepting applications for its Fall 2026 Writing Fellowship, a six-week virtual workshop program connecting writers with established national editors and journalists. Fellows participate in small-group online sessions held Tuesday evenings from September 15 to October 27, 2026, to hone policy, opinion, and journalism writing, learn pitch strategies, and receive direct editorial feedback. The program is remote and designed specifically for writers based outside the Washington, D.C. area who align with the organization's mission. The application deadline is August 25, 2026. Applicants must submit a completed application form, a resume, and two writing samples (preferably published, up to 1,000 words each), with an optional letter of recommendation. Financial compensation, stipends, or participation fees are not stated, making the funding level funding unclear.

art-residencies.headline: Gibbes Museum of Art Society 1858 Prize for Contemporary Southern Art ($10,000)
art-residencies.summary: Presented by the Gibbes Museum of Art and Society 1858, the 18th annual Society 1858 Prize awards $10,000 to one contemporary artist alongside a year-long museum exhibition of their work in Charleston and an invitation to a three-day celebration and forum in February 2027. This prize is open to artists working across all media who currently live or work in, or are originally from, 14 eligible Southern states: Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia. The application deadline has been extended to September 14, 2026. The source specifies the $10,000 award and year-long exhibition; other financial details such as travel stipends or application fees are not stated. The funding is fully funded.
